title: Cold rebuild: comment out a block
summary: Comment out a range of lines in a real script with real Vim, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Undo, dot, registers and visual mode* you commented out a block of a real script
with real Vim. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are
exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson, then try
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: You pressed `dd` five times and deleted one line too many. Which is the quickest correct fix?
steps.explain: Each `dd` is its own change, so one `u` brings back the last line. `p` would paste it below the cursor, possibly in the wrong place.

steps.title: Comment out a block, cold
prompt: Comment out lines 4 to 6 of `~/deploy.sh` with `# `, using Vim from the command line. Nothing else may change, and the script must still parse.
From memory: no hints this time.
